reason: I'll start recovering iron from worn red cells so the marrow can reuse it.
expectation: The recycling cells will break down the worn cells and recover their iron, though I don't know what form it will take.

alternatives.reason: Growing replacement skin cells also fits a goal, but I want to follow the iron route first.

effect: The iron is carried in blood by proteins, so it can now go to the marrow for reuse.
reaction: It was helpful to see that the recovered iron isn't in metallic fragments.
reason: I'll follow the recovered iron to the marrow to make new red blood cells.
expectation: The marrow will use the iron in developing red blood cells, with its supplied nutrients.

alternatives.reason: Skin replacement is another clear goal, but I want to finish the iron route first.

effect: The recovered iron became part of haemoglobin in new red blood cells, completing the iron route. Skin replacement remains.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the iron reused while the marrow stayed intact.
reason: This is the only available combination, and it supplies the dividing skin cells with materials for growth.
expectation: I expect the cells to produce replacement skin cells while some cells remain at the base.

effect: The new cells form below the surface while the base population remains and older cells shed, completing the skin-replacement goal.
reaction: The picture made the ongoing replacement easy to follow.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following recovered iron into new red blood cells was most worthwhile: it showed how material from worn cells gets reused while the marrow remains intact.

leastWorthwhile.text: The skin-growth combination was the least engaging because it was the only available action, although its result clearly showed replacement.

surprise.text: The recovered iron travels in blood carried by proteins rather than as metallic fragments.

arbitrary.text: None felt purposeless: both pairings had clear goals and picture clues. The compatible-action menu did guide the choices, though.

continue.text: I might continue: seeing old-cell material reused was interesting, but I'd hope for more meaningful choices than the final forced combination.
